title: Assessing and treating risk: accept, mitigate, transfer or avoid

videos.script: The shop has a list of things that could go wrong, and a budget that covers maybe three of them. {{list}} So the question is no longer what the risks are. It is which ones come first, and what to do about each. {{order}} You will rank them two ways. First with words, on a grid of likelihood against impact. Then with money, which tells you whether a control costs more than the loss it prevents. {{grid}} Then the four answers to any risk. Reduce it, hand it to somebody else, stop doing the risky thing, or accept it. {{four}} Accepting is a real answer, as long as the right person signs it. The lesson ends with the document that holds all of this together, the risk register. {{register}}
